 AnnaSophia Robb on I Play Rocky and Representing the Underdogs
 Robb talks about showcasing the unrecognized heroes who operate behind the scenes and shining a spotlight on the woman who helped make Rocky happen.
 By
 Patricia Karounos 
 | Published November 18, 2026 
 TAGGED AS: movies 
 (Photo by Steve Granitz/Getty Images) 
 Watching I Play Rocky can feel like you have front row seats to a magic show. The Peter Farrelly -directed drama chronicles the arduous journey it took to make Rocky in the ’70s, and in an uncanny feat of movie trickery, so many of the sequences take you right back to when you first watched the now iconic sports film. Even more wild to behold? Anthony Ippolito’ s total transformation into Sylvester Stallone , who was then a struggling actor and writer who penned the film so that he could star in it. Even those on set got swept up in the illusion. 
 “I felt like I was in the movie [ Rocky ],” says star AnnaSophia Robb , who plays Sasha Czack, then Stallone’s wife and a photographer who also worked on Rocky . “We were filming in Philly and hearing neighbors go, ‘Wow, this brings back a memory.’” 
 BEHIND THE SCENES, FULLY REALIZED  
 (Photo by Claire Folger/©Amazon MGM Studios) 
 Although so much of I Play Rocky is about bringing new depth to a familiar and beloved story, Robb had a dual challenge. One one hand, she was playing a character based on a real-life, an incredibly private person (Robb has not had the chance to meet or speak with Czack) who played a significant role in the making of Rocky . On the other, she wanted to make sure her Sasha was more than just the one-dimensional wife character that is so common in biopics about inspirational men. 
 For Robb, accomplishing both started with research (the actress dug into documentaries, books, and Czack’s photos) and the script, which made the challenge far more approachable. “I thought the dialogue was really truthful. She [felt like] a full person with a full history, ideas, and a future. She’s a real woman, and it felt that way,” she says. 
 Stallone also wrote Robb a note ahead of production describing Sasha as “sunshine” and their relationship as “two rocks leaning against each other,” helping her and Ippolito bring their on-screen romance to life. “Reading the script, I just saw this relationship that I thought was so beautiful,” she says. “This movie is an underdog story. It’s about one man, an artist, believing in himself, and all of the team members it takes to realize that dream. But [Sasha] is the cornerstone.” 
 Even before Czack steps on set with her camera, she’s shown supporting Stallone in his lowest moments, encouraging him to write, typing up his scribbled-on-paper screenplays on a typewriter, and giving him feedback. Czack is perhaps the first person who empowers Stallone to pursue his dreams, helping him trust himself and his talents. And then, along the way, more and more people start believing in him too.
 Whether romantic, platonic, or even professional, that’s the kind of support anyone needs. “You just need someone behind you,” says Robb. “It’s that behind-the-scenes foundation that [helps] people go out and be bold,” she adds. “How exciting [is it] that we get to find out about Sasha — and this type of person who exists for so many people, but who never really gets the attention that they deserve?”
 And while Czack may have been a quiet force behind Rocky , Robb is thrilled that she is getting a piece of the spotlight in I Play Rocky . “There are so many people, especially in the film industry, [who], because they’re not front-facing, don’t get the credit they deserve,” she says. “There are so many fingerprints that go into making a film, so, for me, it’s been a real honor to represent that type of person.”
 THE UNDERDOG CHALLENGE   
 (Photo by ©Amazon MGM Studios) 
 Robb may admit to feeling transported during production, but she also tried to stay focused on the job at hand. That meant thinking about her Sasha as separate from the real-life person and the emotional journey she and Sylvester go on as characters. That also meant staying completely removed from the legacy that Rocky carries. But now that Robb is out of character and is able to talk about I Play Rocky , she’s so moved by seeing how much the original movie still means to people. 
 But, in retrospect, that makes perfect sense. Rocky is a classic because it’s timeless. It’s, as Robb describes it, an underdog story about a boxer who defies the odds and, in the end, realizes that winning isn’t the most important thing — not giving up on yourself and knowing your own heart is. I Play Rocky tugs on those exact strings too, which is why it feels so relevant today even though it’s capturing a period of time in the ’70s. 
 “Our film showcases how many people it takes to make something amazing happen. It starts with one person’s idea,” Robb says. “Then we meet all of the people around this person who made it possible. It’s so important to recognize that great things come from believing in yourself and following that truth. It’s not about money. It’s about doing the right thing and making it happen. We want to believe that we can do hard things and succeed.”
